text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Centre Party, which cooperates informally with Sweden's minority Social Democratic government, keeps losing voter support. In an April survey by pollster Temo, the party was backed by 5.5 percent of voters, down from 6.5 percent in March and seven percent in February.
The Social Democrats have, however, recovered some support, up to 31.5 percent in April from 29.5 percent in March.
- A crisis of confidence between Pharmacia & Upjohn employees and the formerly U.S. dominated company's management is contributing to the share price fall, unions said.
- A computer security head at Swedish state-owned telecoms company Telia spread a virus in the group and to 100 companies in Sweden when he was trying to kill it.
- Sweden's National Board of Health and Welfare proposes stricter sanitary rules at daycare centres to reduce the number of days children are ill.
- Employers dismiss a government forecast that wages will rise close to five percent this year, saying it is too high.
- Truckmaker Scania's first quarter profit after financial items halved to 577 million crowns.

- The idea of forming a pan-Nordic network for gas distribution is back on the agenda after a meeting of the Nordic heads of state this week although Norway's Statoil said it is taking a wait-and-see attitude.
- Merita Bank says in a report on the forestry industry that in nine of the last 10 years forestry companies have failed to earn a return on investment greater than their cost of capital.
- The newspaper said it surveyed local party leaders of the Social Democratic Party which showed they were taking a wait-and-see attitude on EMU.
- Shares in TV4, the largest commercial channel, dropped after a poor first quarter report.
- Lithellsgruppen, owner of the Sibylla fast-food chain, is to form a cooperative of 306 hot-dog stands around Sweden.
